question: In Δ ABC, AD is perpendicular to BC and AE is the bisector of ∠ BAC. If ∠ABC = 58° and ∠ACB = 34°, then find the measure of ∠DAE.
solution:
**Given:**

∠ABC = 58° and ∠ACB = 34°

**Concept used:**

The sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

A bisector of an angle divides the angles into equal parts

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d98ed3530840e1588cce50f9bf77b806d3da6b0b6ce8b1c87905d7da623dcf0a.png] **

In, ΔABC, ∠BAC = 180° - 58° - 34° = 88°

∴ ∠BAE = 88°/2 = 44°

Here, AD ⊥ AC

In ΔBAD, ∠BAD = 180° - 58° - 90° = 32°

So, ∠DAE = ∠BAE - ∠BAD = 44° - 32° = 12°

**∴ The measure of ∠DAE is 12°**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**AD is perpendicular to BC and AE is the bisector of ∠BAC, then

∠DAE = (∠B - ∠C)/2

⇒ (58° - 34°)/2

⇒ 24°/2 = 12°
